chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Indeed, for the servant, half of his prayer, a third, a quarter, or a fifth is raised [accepted], and nothing is raised except what he directed his heart towards during it; and they were commanded to perform the voluntary prayers so that through them what was lacking in the obligatory duty may be completed for them."
ai.seo_question: How is the acceptance of prayer determined by the presence of the heart, and what is the purpose of voluntary prayers?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib-al-ahkam*'s chapter on forgetfulness (*sahw*), this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that prayer acceptance is proportional to the duration of heart-centered presence (*hudhur al-qalb*), rather than mere physical completion. It highlights the theological wisdom behind *nawafil* (voluntary) prayers as a means to rectify the spiritual deficits and lapses in concentration inherent in the obligatory (*fard*) prayers, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the quality of worship.
